description: A single-panel table rendered as an image (no micrograph or curve panels present), titled by the caption "Stress, dislocation density and dislocation substructure size in different strains at RT and LNT". The table has seven columns: a row-label column plus six strain conditions (3.0, 10.0, 20.0, 28.0, 38.0, 55.0 % engineering strain) and ten data rows. Reported quantities are engineering strain (%), true strain (%) rising to 43.8 at the highest condition, true stress (MPa) at RT (339, 483, 635, 723, 800, "–" for 55 %) and at LNT (598, 778, 1007, 1148, 1280, 1463 MPa), geometrically necessary dislocation density ρ^GND from EBSD-α (RT: 0.71→8.99; LNT: 0.97→9.73, in units of 10^14 m^-2), total dislocation density ρ from XRD (RT: 0.64→8.03; LNT: 0.72→13.32, 10^14 m^-2), and cell/ dislocation-cell block size "CBs or DCs size" in nm (RT: 448 ± 74 at 20 % and 282 ± 56 at 28 %; LNT: 429 ± 76 and 242 ± 54 nm). Missing entries are marked "–" or left blank. The table documents that every measured quantity increases monotonically with strain and that LNT values exceed RT values at every shared strain, supporting stronger strain hardening and higher dislocation storage at cryogenic temperature.
measured_quantities: GND dislocation density ρ^GND, EBSD-α (10^14 m^-2)

observations.observation: The figure is a table, not a plot: it contains no axes, curves, scale bars or images, only printed numeric cells with a header row of engineering strains 3.0, 10.0, 20.0, 28.0, 38.0 and 55.0 %.
True stress (RT) is tabulated as 339, 483, 635, 723 and 800 MPa for 3.0-38.0 % engineering strain, with the 55.0 % entry given as a dash (not measured).
True stress (LNT) is tabulated as 598, 778, 1007, 1148, 1280 and 1463 MPa, i.e. higher than the RT value at every strain where both are reported.
ρ^GND (RT-EBSD-α) rises from 0.71 to 8.99 ×10^14 m^-2 between 3.0 and 38.0 % engineering strain, with no value at 55.0 %.
ρ^GND (LNT-EBSD-α) rises from 0.97 to 9.73 ×10^14 m^-2 across the full 3.0-55.0 % strain column set.
ρ (RT-XRD) rises from 0.64 to 8.03 ×10^14 m^-2 and ρ (LNT-XRD) from 0.72 to 13.32 ×10^14 m^-2; the XRD cell for RT at 55.0 % is left blank.
CBs or DCs size is reported only at 20.0 % and 28.0 % strain: 448 ± 74 nm and 282 ± 56 nm at RT, and 429 ± 76 nm and 242 ± 54 nm at LNT.
At both 20.0 % and 28.0 %, the CBs/DCs size is smaller at LNT than at RT, while the ± standard deviations overlap between the two temperatures.
True strain values (3.0, 9.5, 18.2, 24.7, 32.2, 43.8 %) are listed alongside the corresponding engineering strains, so true strain is always lower than engineering strain at the same condition.
The caption states the table reports stress, dislocation density and dislocation substructure size in different strains at RT and LNT.
The caption table lists ρ^GND (RT-EBSD-α) reaching 8.99 ×10^14 m^-2 at 38.0 % and LNT reaching 9.73 ×10^14 m^-2 at 55.0 %, matching the values visible in the image.
The paper abstract identifies the material as a low-carbon low-density steel of Fe35Mn6Al0.1C tested at RT and liquid nitrogen temperature (LNT).

Both GND (EBSD) and total (XRD) dislocation densities increase monotonically with strain, and at every shared strain the LNT value exceeds the RT value, indicating greater dislocation accumulation at cryogenic temperature.

subfigures.description: One tabular panel with no axes or legend: six strain columns (3.0, 10.0, 20.0, 28.0, 38.0, 55.0 % engineering strain) crossed with ten rows giving true strain (%), true stress at RT and LNT (MPa), ρ^GND from RT-EBSD-α and LNT-EBSD-α (10^14 m^-2), ρ from RT-XRD and LNT-XRD (10^14 m^-2), and CBs or DCs size at RT and LNT (nm, with ± standard deviations). Dashes mark unmeasured conditions.
